extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and practitioners preparing submissions (full papers, posters, demos, datasets, tutorials, workshops) for ICWSM-2025
extracted.subtask_description: Conference submission and proposal guidelines for ICWSM-2025 covering formatting, anonymization, ethics checklist, page limits, dataset/poster/demo rules, workshop/tutorial proposal requirements, mentoring, and award nomination/selection criteria. Targets authors and organizers preparing materials for peer review and conference inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting: AAAI two-column US Letter PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers must be submitted as high-resolution PDF files, formatted in AAAI two-column, camera-ready style, for US Letter (8.5" x 11") paper, using Type 1 or TrueType fonts (available templates: AAAI 2025 Author Kit on Overleaf or AAAI 2025 Author Kit.zip [Word | LaTeX]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided templates; submit only high-resolution PDF; no source files (Word or LaTeX) are required at submission; copyright slug may be omitted in initial submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full paper page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Full papers are recommended to be 8 pages long, and must be at most 11 pages long, including only the main text and the references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mandatory Ethics Checklist (and brief additional Ethics Statement, if desired), optional appendices, etc. do not count toward the page limit and should be placed after the references. Revision papers and final camera-ready full papers can be up to 12 pages, not including the Ethics Checklist and optional appendices. Note that reviewers are not bound to review appendices, and excessively long appendices can be a ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics Checklist is mandatory and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to include a checklist that describes the potential broader impact of their work and ethical considerations (the Paper Checklist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This completed and unaltered checklist should come as the first section after the references of the paper. Authors may supplement the Paper Checklist with a brief discussion in the same section. This section does not count towards the page limit, and papers without such a statement will be desk-rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All submission must be in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity and double-blind review
rubrics_metrics.description: ICWSM-2025 review is double-blind. Therefore, please anonymize your submission: do not put the author names or affiliations at the start of the paper, and do not include funding or other acknowledgments in papers submitted for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to authors' own prior relevant work should be included, but should not specify that this is the authors' own work. It is up to the authors' discretion how much to further modify the body of the paper to preserve anonymity. The requirement for anonymity does not extend outside of the review process. Exception: 2-page demo submissions and dataset paper submissions are exempt from the anonymization requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission requirements for Revise & Resubmit
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that were previously submitted to ICWSM and received a 'Revise and Resubmit' decision should be accompanied by a copy of the previous reviews and an author response statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The response statement may be in any format, but a suggested helpful format is an overall summary followed by a table mapping each reviewer comment to the author's response (explain why no changes were made or describe changes and direct reviewers to the revised material). The revised version may be sent back to some or all original reviewers at the Senior PC member's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: File types at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Only high-resolution PDF files are permitted at submission time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No source files (Word or LaTeX) are required for review; the copyright slug may be omitted in the initial submission phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of funding and competing interests (camera-ready)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are required to provide an explicit disclosure of funding (financial activities supporting the submitted work) and competing interests (related financial activities outside the submitted work) that could result in conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure should be added to the camera-ready version (e.g., in 'Acknowledgments') but not in the version submitted for review to maintain anonymity. Authors are also required to read the AAAI code of conduct and ethics guidelines; submitting implies agreement to abide by these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission timing rule for rejected full papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of rejected papers from ICWSM may revise and submit their revised papers after 6 months of the date of the last decision, but not before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limit only applies to rejected full papers, and not to rejected demo, poster, or dataset papers. Example: papers submitted in the January round can be resubmitted to the September round (6 months after the decision in March) but not the May round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI use and authorship policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI tools and technologies may not be listed as authors of an ACM published Work. The use of generative AI tools and technologies to create content is permitted but must be fully disclosed in the Work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors could include a disclosure statement (example provided) in the Acknowledgements. Basic word processing systems that recommend/insert replacement text, perform spelling/grammar checks, or do language translations are exceptions and generally need not be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: ICWSM-2025 will not accept any paper that, at the time of submission, is under review for or has already been published or accepted for publication in a journal or conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction does not apply to submissions for non-archival workshops. If duplicate submissions are identified during the review process then: all submissions from that author will be disqualified from the current ICWSM conference and authors will not be permitted to submit papers to the ICWSM conference in the following year. Note: social sciences and sociophysics (not for publication) may be under review concurrently at a journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance outcomes and revision opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who receive the 'Accept' recommendation will have the opportunity to respond to reviewer suggestions by making minor edits preparing camera-ready. Authors who receive the 'Revise and Resubmit' recommendation will have the opportunity to address reviewer suggestions and resubmit in the next submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers accepted no later than March will be presented at the conference that year and published in proceedings. Authors who receive R&R in March will likely present in the following year's conference if accepted in the next round.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices review and length caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices (placed after the Ethics Checklist) do not count toward page limit and may include additional material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are not bound to review appendices, and excessively long appendices can be a ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poster submission formatting and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Poster papers must be no longer than 5 pages (excluding the mandatory ethics checklist and optional appendices), with page 5 containing nothing but references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posters must follow the same formatting guidelines as full papers (2-column). Poster submissions are double-blind. The reviewing process for posters results in accept or reject; there is no revise-and-resubmit phase. Reviewers may not be bound to read appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demo submission formatting and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Demo descriptions must be no longer than 3 pages (excluding the mandatory ethics checklist and optional appendices), with page 3 containing nothing but references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demos must follow the same formatting (2-column). Demo submissions are single-blind and require the Ethics Checklist. Demos have accept/reject decisions with no revise-and-resubmit phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset paper length and review model
rubrics_metrics.description: Dataset paper submissions must be between 2-10 pages long, including references but excluding the mandatory 'Ethics Checklist' section, and will be part of the full proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions will either be accepted or rejected without an option to revise and resubmit. The review will be single-blind, and all datasets must be identified and uploaded at the time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset content and metadata requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must comprise (i) a dataset or group of datasets, and (ii) a paper describing the content, quality, structure, potential uses of the dataset(s), as well as the methodology employed for data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive statistics may be included in the metadata; more sophisticated analyses should be included in regular paper submissions. Datasets and metadata must be published using a dataset-sharing service (e.g., Zenodo, datatorium, dataverse) that provides a DOI, which must be included in the dataset paper submission. Authors are encouraged to include a small sample of the dataset (maximum of 10MB, in csv, txt, json, or other readable formats) as supplementary material to aid reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR and Datasheets recommendations for datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to include a description of how they intend to make their datasets FAIR and to consider addressing the questions covered in the Datasheets for Datasets recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop proposal scope and selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops should be kept small (up to 40 participants) and provide an informal setting for active exchange; two main criteria for selection are: potential to attract interest of researchers in computer science and social science, and interdisciplinarity/organizer diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers are encouraged to propose interactive activities (challenges, games, brainstorming, networking). Organizers should avoid mini-conference formats dominated by long talks and short discussions, and should leave ample time for discussions and interaction. Proposals that involve people of different backgrounds in the organizing committee and address topics at the intersection of disciplines will have a higher chance of acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop proposal content and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for workshops should be no more than five (5) pages (10pt, single column), written in English, and contain: concise title; names/affiliations/contact info of organizers; main contact; half-day/full-day indication; short abstract; 2-3 paragraph description of topic/themes; description of format and activities; approximate timeline; description of how submissions will be evaluated/selected; historical information; list of related workshops and differences; short bios for organizers; brief statement on generative AI use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PC is needed, provide tentative list of members. Strong proposals include organizers who bring differing perspectives and are connected to potential participants. Workshop organizers who want to publish workshop papers may do so via AAAI Press proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tutorial proposal types and acceptance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: ICWSM seeks tutorials in several formats (lecture-style, hands-on, translation, case study, free-style) and proposals will be selected considering relevance/interest/value, cross-pollination potential, interactivity, completeness/clarity/quality of proposal and materials (including schedule), and expertise of presenters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty is a plus. The tutorial chairs may contact proposers about changing duration to fit program needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tutorial proposal content and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for tutorials should be no more than three (3) pages and include: title; abstract (200 words) for website; tutorial type; names/affiliations/emails/websites of organizers (main contact); duration and timeline; tutorial schedule and detailed description of activities; target audience, prerequisites and outcomes; list of materials to be made available; past precedent (if available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For hands-on tutorials include OS and required tools, software licenses required, and setup instructions (setup should not take more than 1 hour). Use AAAI 2025 Author Kit templates and email a single file to tutorial chairs before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring scheme eligibility and process
rubrics_metrics.description: The mentoring scheme supports first-time ICWSM authors: interested authors can submit a complete manuscript by a specified date to receive written feedback from a Senior PC member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submitting, authors must confirm: none of the authors has any prior ICWSM full papers (poster/dataset/workshop excluded); manuscript is complete (typically 7-11 pages); availability to substantially revise between feedback and resubmission deadline; manuscript presents research related to 'the Web and social media'. Priority given to first authors from low/lowermiddle/uppermiddle income economies per World Bank classification and to authors without prior ICWSM experience. Mentoring capacity is limited; mentoring does not guarantee acceptance; revised papers will be handled by different SPC member who won't see mentoring history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop/tutorial AI disclosure and discouragement of AI-generated ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop proposals should include a brief statement on whether any generative AI tools were used to generate ideas for the workshop or the workshop activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshop organizers strongly discourage the use of generative AI to come up with workshop ideas and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedural steps (PCS selection)
rubrics_metrics.description: To submit, register/login to PCS account; click Submissions tab and select from dropdown menus: Society: AAAI. Conference/Journal: ICWSM 25. Track: ICWSM 25 [appropriate track]. After clicking 'Go' a placeholder submission will appear; click 'Edit Submission' to add paper details. The submission will be marked complete when all required fields are entered but can be edited until submissions close.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate tracks exist for full papers and for posters/demos/datasets. Use the correct track for the type of submission (e.g., 'ICWSM 25 Posters, Demos, and Datasets').

rubrics_metrics.name: Adamic-Glance Distinguished Early Career Award: eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The award is open to individuals who have received their PhD within the past 10 years (career interruptions and other special circumstances will be considered), perform research recognizably within social computing/computational social science, and have published research in top venues and participated in ICWSM through community service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As long as a candidate is eligible based on these criteria, they will be considered even if nominated in prior years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adamic-Glance Award: nomination materials and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations solicit a statement (no longer than two pages) explaining why the nominee deserves the award, highlighting novelty and strength, and evidence of academic and societal impact; citations for up to three representative publications and/or links to artefacts; letters of support may be submitted, but the committee will limit consideration to three letters of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee will contact nominated individuals and may suggest they submit a two-page narrative of research contributions. The nomination form requires nominator and nominee information; letters from others can be uploaded directly. The nomination form requires Google authentication; email acceptance provided if that is a problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adamic-Glance Award: selection criteria and COI
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection is based on the impact of the candidate's work: identifying significant new problems, creating promising new ideas, paradigms, and tools related to data-driven understanding of human behavior. Depth and impact are valued over breadth; a strong regard for ethical aspects of data/methods is expected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection committee members recuse themselves for nominees who are former or current collaborators. Award recipients will join the award committee within two years to replace rotating members.
